heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Costa Rica
heroData.subtitle: Compliant hiring solution without a local entity
heroData.description: Hire talent in Costa Rica within days using our Employer of Record (EOR) services. We handle all local compliance, from CCSS social security to Aguinaldo bonuses, so you can focus on growth.
heroData.bestFor: Companies seeking rapid market entry (1-10 employees)

steps.title: Employment Contract Execution
steps.description: Drafting of bilingual (Spanish/English) contracts that strictly adhere to the Costa Rican Labor Code. Contracts must specify the 'jornada' (work shift) and salary in CRC or USD.

steps.title: CCSS & INS Registration
steps.description: Mandatory enrollment with the Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social (CCSS) for health/pension and the Instituto Nacional de Seguros (INS) for occupational risk insurance.

steps.title: Background & Reference Checks
steps.description: Verification of academic credentials and prior employment history, often required for specialized and management roles in San José's tech hubs.

steps.title: Digital Signature Setup
steps.description: Assisting employees in obtaining a 'Firma Digital' if they need to sign official government documents or manage municipal permits on behalf of the company.

steps.title: Equipment & IT Provisioning
steps.description: Coordination of laptop delivery and secure VPN access, ensuring compliance with local data privacy standards and home office stipend requirements.

items.title: Just Cause Termination
items.text: Costa Rica is highly pro-employee. Terminating without 'Justa Causa' requires payment of 'Cesantía' (severance), which can be up to 22 days per year of service.

items.title: Aguinaldo Deadline
items.text: The 13th-month salary (Aguinaldo) must be paid between December 1st and December 20th. Failure to meet this deadline leads to heavy fines from the Ministry of Labor.

items.title: Work Shift Flexibility
items.text: Utilize the 'Jornada Acumulativa' (cumulative shift) to allow 48 hours of work in 5 days instead of 6, a common practice to attract top talent who prefer weekends off.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in USD?
faqs.answer: Yes, salaries can be negotiated and paid in USD, but social security (CCSS) and income tax (Hacienda) must be calculated and reported based on the BCCR exchange rate on the date of payment.

faqs.question: What is the standard probation period?
faqs.answer: The maximum legal probation period in Costa Rica is 3 months. During this time, either party can terminate the contract without notice or severance pay.

faqs.question: Is health insurance provided through the EOR?
faqs.answer: The CCSS (Caja) provides universal healthcare. While mandatory, many EOR clients also offer private supplemental insurance (e.g., Pan-American or BlueCross) as a perk.

items.title: The 'Pura Vida' Culture
items.text: Business interactions are polite and relationship-oriented. Start meetings with small talk to build rapport before diving into technical agendas.

items.title: Education Hubs
items.text: San José and Heredia (Free Zones) are the primary talent hubs. The University of Costa Rica (UCR) and TEC are the top sources for engineering and tech talent.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: Costa Rica has the highest fiber-optic penetration in Central America, making it ideal for remote teams working for US/Canada firms.

steps.title: Gross Salary Calculation
steps.description: Aggregating base pay, overtime (paid at 1.5x), and any taxable allowances like housing or transportation.

steps.title: CCSS Retentions
steps.description: Calculating the mandatory 10.67% employee deduction for health, disability, and old-age pensions.

steps.title: Income Tax Withholding (I.S.T.)
steps.description: Applying the progressive tax brackets (0% to 25%) based on the monthly salary thresholds defined by Hacienda.

steps.title: Net Disbursement
steps.description: Executing bank transfers via SINPE (local real-time transfer system) to employee accounts in CRC or USD.

steps.title: Statutory Reporting
steps.description: Electronic filing of the 'Planilla Digital' with CCSS and the monthly tax declaration (D-103) with Hacienda.

items.title: SINPE System
items.text: The 'Sistema Nacional de Pagos Electrónicos' (SINPE) is the backbone of local payments. Ensure your payroll software integrates with SINPE to avoid 24-hour clearing delays.

items.title: Overtime Caps
items.text: Employees cannot exceed 12 hours of total daily work (8 regular + 4 overtime). Exceeding this triggers significant penalties and legal risk during labor audits.

items.title: Aguinaldo Provisions
items.text: Account for the 8.33% Accrued Aguinaldo monthly in your financial statements to avoid year-end cash flow shocks in December.

faqs.question: What is the fiscal year in Costa Rica?
faqs.answer: The fiscal year for individuals and companies runs from January 1st to December 31st.

faqs.question: Are fringe benefits taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, benefits like company cars or housing allowances are generally treated as 'Salario en Especie' (salary in kind) and are subject to CCSS and income tax.

faqs.question: How do I handle sick leave payments?
faqs.answer: For the first 3 days, the employer pays 50% and CCSS pays 50%. After the 4th day, CCSS pays 60% and the employer pays nothing (though some offer top-ups).

steps.title: Input Gross Monthly Salary
steps.description: The user enters the monthly base salary in Costa Rican Colones (CRC) or USD equivalent.

steps.title: Social Security Application
steps.description: The calculator automatically deducts 10.67% from the employee and calculates the 26.67% employer liability for CCSS.

steps.title: Progressive Tax Slicing
steps.description: The logic applies the current Hacienda brackets (e.g., 10% above 929k per month) to find the net withholding.

steps.title: Aguinaldo & Holiday Provision
steps.description: An additional 8.33% is added to the 'Total Employer Cost' to reflect the mandatory Christmas bonus accrual.

steps.title: Final Cost Simulation
steps.description: Output showing: Total Net Pay to Employee vs Total Disbursement for Employer per month.

items.title: Exchange Rate Volatility
items.text: Our calculator uses the Official BCCR 'Venta' rate. We recommend adding a 2% buffer for payrolls funded from foreign accounts to cover bank spread.

items.title: Ceiling for CCSS
items.text: Certain components of social security have a 'Tope' (ceiling) on high salaries. Our calculator logic adjusts for these caps automatically.

items.title: Family Credits
items.text: Don't forget to deduct 'Créditos Familiares' (approx $3 - $5 per month for spouse/children) to slightly reduce the net income tax.

faqs.question: Is Aguinaldo included in the Net Pay?
faqs.answer: No, Aguinaldo is a separate payment in December. The calculator shows the monthly *accrual* cost for budgeting purposes.

faqs.question: Does it handle 'Professional Services'?
faqs.answer: No, this calculator is for 'Relación de Dependencia' (Employees). Independent contractors have different tax rules (2% - 25% on gross).

faqs.question: Are the 2025 brackets updated?
faqs.answer: Yes, our engine is updated every January following Hacienda's official decree on the 'Tramas de Impuesto sobre la Renta'.

items.title: Double Time
items.text: Work performed on mandatory holidays (Feriados de Pago Obligatorio) is paid at 2x the normal rate. Our calculator accounts for this in 'Advanced Mode'.

items.title: Night Shift Premium
items.text: The 'Jornada Nocturna' is limited to 6 hours per day. Pay rates are the same, but the hourly cost is effectively higher due to the shorter shift.

items.title: Aguinaldo Calculation
items.text: Aguinaldo is the sum of all ordinary and extraordinary wages (overtime, commissions, bonuses) divided by 12.

heroData.title: Business Incorporation in Costa Rica
heroData.subtitle: Setup your SA or SRL entity with expert guidance
heroData.description: Establish a legal presence in Costa Rica's booming economy. From drafting articles of incorporation to obtaining your NIF and municipal licenses, we simplify the path to doing business in Central America.
heroData.bestFor: Investors seeking long-term operations and property ownership

steps.title: Selection of Entity Type
steps.description: Choosing between a Sociedad Anónima (SA) for complex ownership structures or a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SRL) for simpler, managerial control.

steps.title: Articles of Incorporation (Notary)
steps.description: Drafting the 'Escritura Pública' by a licensed Costa Rican notary. This document defines the board, resident agent, and share capital.

steps.title: National Registry Filing
steps.description: Electronic submission to the Registro Nacional. Registration of the company name, ID (Cédula Jurídica), and official books.

steps.title: NIF & Hacienda Registration
steps.description: Enrolling in the 'Registro Único Tributario' (RUT) to obtain a tax identification number and enable electronic invoicing.

steps.title: Shareholder Disclosure (RTBF)
steps.description: Mandatory annual reporting of the 'Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiarios Finales' to the Central Bank via digital signature.

items.title: Firma Digital Requirement
items.text: The 'Firma Digital' is essential for legal representatives. Without it, you must grant Power of Attorney (POA) to a local lawyer for almost all administrative tasks.

items.title: Free Trade Zones (FTZ)
items.text: If exporting services or manufacturing, consider registering under the FTZ regime (Ley de Zonas Francas) for 100% corporate tax exemption for up to 8 years.

items.title: Inactive Companies
items.text: Even if your company doesn't generate income, you MUST file the D-195 asset declaration annually. Failure results in fines exceeding $1,000.

faqs.question: How long does it take to register a company?
faqs.answer: With the digital 'Crear Empresa' platform, the process can take as little as 24-48 hours once the notary submits the documents.

faqs.question: Do I need a local partner?
faqs.answer: No, 100% foreign ownership is allowed for both SA and SRL entities. No residency is required for shareholders.

faqs.question: What is a Resident Agent?
faqs.answer: A Resident Agent is a mandatory Costa Rican attorney who receives official legal notifications if the company's representatives do not live in the country.

items.title: Retention is Key
items.text: The market is highly competitive. To retain talent, companies offer 'Asociaciones Solidaristas' (savings funds) and flexible Friday schedules ('viernes corto').

items.title: Nearshoring Advantage
items.text: Costa Rica shares the CST/EST time zone with the US, making it superior to Eastern European or Asian hubs for real-time collaboration.

items.title: Misclassification Risk
items.text: Hiring 'Independent Contractors' for full-time roles is risky. Labors courts often rule these as hidden employment, triggering retroactive benefits.

faqs.question: Where is the best talent located?
faqs.answer: The 'GAM' (Gran Área Metropolitana), specifically San José, Heredia, and Alajuela, holds 85% of the professional workforce.

faqs.question: What are common employee perks?
faqs.answer: Private medical insurance, lunch subsidies (tickets), gym memberships, and performance-based bonuses are standard for top-tier firms.

faqs.question: How long is the notice period for resignation?
faqs.answer: Employees must give 1 month of notice for service over 1 year. During this month, they are entitled to one paid day off per week.

items.title: English Proficiency
items.text: Costa Rica consistently ranks #1 or #2 in Latin America for English proficiency, especially in technical and service sectors.

items.title: Solidarist Associations
items.text: A unique Costa Rican benefit where the employer and employee contribute to a fund for loans, housing, and social events.

items.title: Criminal Record Checks
items.text: Standard practice includes requesting a 'Hoja de Delincuencia' from the Judicial Power during the final stages of recruitment.

items.title: Cloud vs On-Premise
items.text: Cloud-based HRIS is the standard due to Costa Rica's high-speed internet. On-premise solutions are rarely recommended for service-based nearshoring.

items.title: Data Sovereignty
items.text: Ensure your provider is GDPR compliant or follows Costa Rica's 'Ley de Protección de la Persona frente al Tratamiento de sus Datos Personales'.

items.title: Mobile ESS
items.text: Employee Self-Service (ESS) on mobile is mandatory for employee engagement. Most Costa Rican workers manage their personal admin via smartphones.

faqs.question: Does the system handle partial vacation days?
faqs.answer: Yes, our recommended systems allow for tracking the 12-day vacation entitlement down to half-day increments, as allowed by local custom.

faqs.question: Can I integrate my clocking hardware?
faqs.answer: We support integration with biometric (fingerprint/facial) and RFID systems commonly used for physical access control in Heredia's business parks.

faqs.question: Is the interface available in Spanish?
faqs.answer: All HRIS solutions provide 100% Spanish-language interfaces for the workforce, which is critical for legal and cultural reasons.

items.title: Incentivize Profile Completion
items.text: Run a 'Pura Vida' contest where the first department to reach 100% profile completion wins a team lunch.

items.title: Bilingual Support
items.text: Ensure your HRIS helpdesk provides support in Spanish to assist local employees with complex benefit queries.

items.title: Mobile Accessibility
items.text: 90% of employees in Costa Rica will access the HRIS via mobile. Test specifically on mid-range Android devices common in the region.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in Costa Rica
heroData.subtitle: IFRS Compliant Bookkeeping & Financial Reporting
heroData.description: Maintain impeccable financial records in Costa Rica. Our CPA-led services ensure your books stay compliant with IFRS standards and Hacienda's electronic reporting mandates.

steps.title: Document Collection (Factura Electrónica)
steps.description: Automated gathering of XML and PDF versions of all electronic invoices, which are mandatory for tax deductibility.

steps.title: Account Reconciliation
steps.description: Monthly matching of local bank statements (CRC/USD/EUR) with GL entries to ensure 100% accuracy.

steps.title: VAT & Rental Tax Filing
steps.description: Preparation of form D-101 (VAT) and other specific retentions due by the 15th of every month.

steps.title: Financial Statement Preparation
steps.description: Generating Balance Sheets and P&L reports compliant with IFRS for SMEs or Full IFRS for large corporations.

steps.title: Legal Ledger Maintenance
steps.description: Updating and notarizing the physical or digital 'Libros Legales' (Shareholders, Directors, and Minutes) required by law.

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Costa Rica has fully adopted IFRS. Financial statements must follow these global standards to be accepted by banks and tax authorities.

items.title: Electronic Invoicing (FE)
items.text: Any expense not backed by a valid 'Factura Electrónica' XML file is non-deductible for income tax purposes, regardless of a physical receipt.

items.title: Currency Diversification
items.text: Manage your books in both CRC and USD. While the CRC is the legal currency, most high-value transactions and payroll in tech are USD-denominated.

faqs.question: What is the D-101 form?
faqs.answer: The D-101 is the annual Income Tax return form that summarizes all taxable income and expenses for the fiscal year.

faqs.question: Do I need to hire a CPA?
faqs.answer: Yes, annual financial statements for most corporations and all reports for public entities must be signed by a 'Contador Público Autorizado' (CPA).

faqs.question: Are digital books allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, recent regulations allow for digital 'Libros de Legalización' provided they are properly registered with the Tax Administration.

items.title: Periodic Inventories
items.text: Hacienda requires companies to perform at least one physical inventory count per year for tax-deductible status.

items.title: Depreciation Standards
items.text: Ensure your depreciation schedules align with the 'Anexo 1' of the Income Tax Regulation for both accounting and tax purposes.

items.title: Fixed Asset Records
items.text: Maintain a digital registry of all company equipment (laptops, furniture) linked to their corresponding Electronic Invoices (XML).

steps.title: Regulatory Inventory
steps.description: Mapping all required permits including Sanitary Permits (Ministerio de Salud) and Patent (Municipal license).

steps.title: Data Privacy Mapping
steps.description: Reviewing data flows to ensure compliance with Law 8968, registering databases with PRODHAB if necessary.

steps.title: AML/CFT Controls Check
steps.description: Establishing 'Know Your Client' (KYC) protocols for companies in real estate, law, or financial sectors per Law 7786.

steps.title: Shareholder Reporting (RTBF)
steps.description: Uploading the Transparency Registry data to the Central Bank's platform (Central Directo) using a secure digital signature.

steps.title: Internal Policy Training
steps.description: Training local staff on anti-bribery (Law 9699) and ethics policies to avoid corporate criminal liability.

items.title: PRODHAB Registration
items.text: If you process personal data for third parties, you must register your database. Fines for leaks or misuse of data are extremely high in 2025.

items.title: Criminal Liability
items.text: Law 9699 holds companies (not just individuals) liable for bribery of domestic and foreign public officials. Establishing a compliance officer is now a best practice.

items.title: Municipal Patent Licensing
items.text: The 'Patente de Funcionamiento' cost is based on gross income. Optimize your accounting structure to ensure you are accurately reporting locally-derived vs export income.

faqs.question: What is the 'Libro de Actas'?
faqs.answer: It is the official physical or digital book where all shareholder and director meeting minutes must be legally recorded.

faqs.question: Who can register the company with RTBF?
faqs.answer: Only the legal representative with a valid Costa Rican digital signature can perform this filing directly.

faqs.question: What is SUGEF and do I need it?
faqs.answer: SUGEF is the financial regulator. You only need registration if you are a bank, lender, or handling financial assets for third parties.

items.title: Occupational Risk (INS)
items.text: Every employer must have a valid INS policy. Failure to pay monthly premiums results in immediate suspension of business activities during inspections.

items.title: Ergonomics & Home Office
items.text: For remote teams, the Ministry of Labor now checks for 'Teletrabajo' compliance, including ergonomic standards for at-home setups.

items.title: Emergency Committees
items.text: Offices with more than 10 employees must have an internal 'Comisión de Salud Ocupacional' registered with the government.

steps.title: Fiscal Opening
steps.description: Updating economic activity codes (CIIU) and registering any new branches or digital platforms with Hacienda.

steps.title: VAT Reporting (Monthly)
steps.description: Filing the D-101 (IVA) by the 15th of the following month, ensuring all input and output credits are matched via XML.

steps.title: Advance Tax Payments
steps.description: Calculation and payment of quarterly income tax advances required by the DGT for active businesses.

steps.title: Annual Income Return (D-101)
steps.description: Consolidated reporting of the year's P&L and calculation of final corporate tax due at the end of the fiscal year.

steps.title: Informative Returns (D-151)
steps.description: Reporting annual transactions with major suppliers and clients to Hacienda to prevent tax evasion.

items.title: Territoriality Principle
items.text: Costa Rica only taxes income generated within its borders. While this is changing due to OECD pressure, foreign-source income is generally exempt if properly structured.

items.title: Global Minimum Tax
items.text: Costa Rica is aligning with the OECD Pillar Two 15% global minimum tax, which may impact multinational tax planning in the next 12-24 months.

items.title: Withholding Tax (WHT)
items.text: Dividends sent abroad are subject to a 15% WHT. Check for Double Taxation Treaties (e.g., CR-UAE, CR-Germany) to reduce this to 5% or 10%.

faqs.question: What is the 'Cédula Jurídica'?
faqs.answer: The Cédula Jurídica is your company's permanent tax ID. It is required for all banking, contracts, and filings.

faqs.question: Is there a tax on inactive companies?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Personas Jurídicas' must pay an annual tax of approx. $120-$400 even if they don't operate.

faqs.question: Are salaries spent abroad deductible?
faqs.answer: Only if they are necessary to generate Costa Rican source income and have the appropriate WHT applied if paid to non-residents.

items.title: Standard Withholding
items.text: A flat 15% rate applies to dividends paid to both local and foreign shareholders unless a tax treaty specifies otherwise.

items.title: Free Zone Advantage
items.text: Companies under the Free Trade Zone regime (Regimen de Zona Franca) may benefit from exemption or reduced rates on dividend withholding.

items.title: Pillar Two Readiness
items.text: MNCs should prepare for the 15% global minimum tax reporting even if they currently operate under full tax holiday regimes.

items.title: Arbitration in Costa Rica

items.title: Service Agreements vs Employment
items.text: Ensure your MSA doesn't inadvertently create an employment relationship. Avoid clauses that specify hours of work or direct supervision of individual vendor staff.

items.title: Digital Contracts
items.text: Contracts signed using international e-signature platforms (Docusign/HelloSign) are legally valid in CRC commercial law since 2021.

faqs.question: Which language should the MSA be in?
faqs.answer: For commercial use, English is standard. However, if the contract must be produced in court, a certified translation to Spanish will be required.

faqs.question: Can I use 'Unilateral Termination'?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard 30, 60, or 90-day 'Without Cause' termination notice periods are enforceable and common in tech MSAs.

faqs.question: Are Non-Compete clauses legal in CR?
faqs.answer: They are difficult to enforce for individuals unless compensated, but Non-Solicitation of clients/staff at the B2B level is standard and enforceable.

items.title: Standard Notice Period
items.text: A 30-day notice period is standard in B2B service agreements, though complex enterprise MSAs often extend this to 90 days for business continuity.

items.title: Liquidation Damages
items.text: Penalty clauses for early termination by the client are legal but must be 'reasonable' to avoid being struck down by commercial courts.

items.title: Post-Termination Support
items.text: Always define a 'Knowledge Transfer' phase of at least 2 weeks to ensure smooth transition of source code or confidential data back to the client.
